payload.analysis: Combined with suspected ear syringing injury/infection, CT shows left middle ear/mastoid fluid without bone erosion; audiometry and tympanometry confirm mixed hearing loss and tympanic membrane perforation, supporting traumatic perforation with secondary otitis media/mastoiditis. payload.report: Post-syringing onset, ENT-visible anteroinferior TM perforation, CT middle ear/mastoid fluid, and audiometry/tympanometry confirming middle ear dysfunction point to traumatic TM perforation with secondary otitis media/mastoiditis from ear syringing. Isolated otitis externa is refuted by middle ear involvement. The facial palsy reflects inflammatory facial nerve involvement secondary to this infection. Primary otitis media is less likely given temporal relationship. Missing culture and facial nerve MRI leave residual uncertainty; diagnosis explains evidence.
